text:
I’m stepping away from X for a while, and I hope I can spend the next year focusing on college, studying, learning, and understanding the world instead of constantly trying to change it.

This is harder than I expected, because I genuinely enjoy being here. Not because of followers or attention, but because I love reading people’s thoughts and offering a perspective they might never have considered. I like thinking that maybe somebody will read something I wrote, try something different, and experience the kind of life I’ve finally started living. If I help one person, and that person helps three more, perhaps I’ve made a difference. That’s always been my motivation.

For years, I lived exhausted. Now I wake up naturally, clearheaded, curious, and ready to enjoy another day. I have more time and mental energy than I know what to do with. And I keep wanting to use that energy to help other people understand that they might not need another supplement, injection, medication, or some new explanation for everything they’re experiencing. Perhaps they need to start by investigating something as ordinary as the quality of their sleep.

I believe we’ve overlooked what generations of changes to our jaws, airways, and the way we develop physically may have done to our ability to breathe properly at night. You can sleep eight hours and still have your brain repeatedly waking you up just enough to keep breathing. You won’t necessarily remember it happening, but those interruptions can leave you exhausted the next day. I know what happened when I finally addressed my own nighttime breathing, and I wish everyone could experience the difference.

And there I go again as I’m supposed to be writing a goodbye, and I’m already trying to explain something I want everyone to understand.

That’s exactly why I need to step away.

These websites are incredibly good at keeping us engaged. There’s always another opinion, another person to respond to, another opportunity to feel like we’re doing something meaningful. And sometimes we really are helping. But somewhere along the way, I’ve started spending more time responding to other people’s thoughts than developing my own.

I don’t want to spend the next year trying to convince strangers that I’ve figured something out. I want to spend it learning how much I still don’t know. I want to study human behavior, history, anthropology, biology, and the many things that make us who we are. I want to have real conversations, meet interesting people, and experience the world rather than spend so much of my day looking at it through a screen.

If I could leave one piece of advice, it would be to investigate your sleep. Not just how many hours you’re getting, but whether those hours are actually restorative. Ask about a proper sleep study that records brain activity through EEG and examines breathing-related microarousals, not just whether you stop breathing. For me, discovering that my breathing was disrupting my sleep and finding a mouthpiece that helped changed my experience of everyday life.

I spent so many years exhausted that I didn’t understand what it was like to wake up feeling good. Now that I do, I want to appreciate it. I want to enjoy people, learn from them, travel, study, and see what else life has to offer.

I still want to help others, and I probably always will. But I don’t have to change the world today. I have a lot more living and learning to do before I can truly understand the things I want to share.

So this isn’t a sad goodbye. It’s simply me choosing to spend the time I’ve gained actually living.

I’ll be back someday. Hopefully with a little more knowledge, a few more experiences, and something worth sharing.

text:
88. 

Al-Ghani / Al-Ghaniyy
(The Self-Sufficient)

Al-Ghani Meaning:
The Rich, The Independent One, The Wealthy.

Allah سُبْحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ is Al-Ghaniyy (in Arabic: ٱلْغَنيُّ), He is The One who is self-sufficient and independent. He does not need anything as He is completely satisfied and free from dependence. Allah is The One whose wealth and riches all others depend on.

Mentions of Al-Ghani:
From Quran & Hadith
Arabic Root:
From the root ghayn-nun-ya (غ ن ي), which has the following classical Arabic connotations: to be free from wants or needs, to be self-sufficient, independent, to be able to do without help from others, to be content, satisfied to be rich, wealthy, flourishing.

The name of Allah سُبْحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ Al-Ghani, the rich or wealthy. This is one of the names of Allah سُبْحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ from the Qur'an as it is mentioned 18 times. It is often explained in pairs with Al-Mughni (The Enricher) for its closeness in meaning. But just as a note to self, Al-Mughni is one of the names where there isn't a consensus as being accepted as an official name of Allah as it's not mentioned in the Qur'an.

The word ghni (غْنِيَ) is often said to imply rich or wealthy. In the Qur'an, "Allah has certainly heard the statement of those [Jews] who said, innal laaha faqeerunw wa nahnu aghniyaaa "Indeed, Allah is poor, while we are rich." (Qur'an 3:181). In a hadith qudsi, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ related Allah سُبْحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ as saying, "[...] O My servants, were the first of you and the last of you, the human of you and the jinn of you to rise up in one place and make a request of Me, and were I to give everyone what he requested, that would not decrease what I have, any more that a needle decreases the sea if put into it."[1] This is how vast Allah سُبْحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ wealth is. If every creation, human and jinn, both past, and present, were to ask Allah سُبْحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ their innermost desire, and He was to give it to you, it would deplete Him as much as if you were to dip a needle in the ocean and try and remove some water with it. This is how rich Al-Ghaniyy is. His ability to provide is non-diminishable.

Living the rich life:
Now, if you were to ask Allah سُبْحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ to gift you with a rich life, what would that mean? One dimension may include monetary success. But if that's all you care about, you'll have missed the aim of what a truly rich life is. Imagine a person who's been given wealth by Allah سُبْحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ but with it a short lifespan, health problems, minimal love and support from friends or family, with limited capacity to think and reason. Would you say they are living a rich life? Their wish will have been wasted as they haven't even considered the purpose of their existence, which is to glorify and worship Allah سُبْحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ. They'll go through their entire life aimlessly, and on the day of resurrection, they'll be lost.

This is to illustrate that when we refer to Al-Ghani as rich, we don't mean in one aspect. But rather, He is abundant in all respects (i.e., knowledge, power, influence, might, time, etc.) In this light, we can see why Al-Ghaniy is often translated as 'The Self-Sufficient.' He is without the need for anything as He has it all. He is independent and entirely satisfied.

قَالَ ٱلَّذِي عِندَهُۥ عِلۡمٞ مِّنَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ أَنَا۠ ءَاتِيكَ بِهِۦ قَبۡلَ أَن يَرۡتَدَّ إِلَيۡكَ طَرۡفُكَۚ فَلَمَّا رَءَاهُ مُسۡتَقِرًّا عِندَهُۥ قَالَ هَٰذَا مِن فَضۡلِ رَبِّي لِيَبۡلُوَنِيٓ ءَأَشۡكُرُ أَمۡ أَكۡفُرُۖ وَمَن شَكَرَ فَإِنَّمَا يَشۡكُرُ لِنَفۡسِهِۦۖ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ رَبِّي غَنِيّٞ كَرِيمٞ
Qaalal lazee indahoo ‘ilmum minal Kitaabi ana aateeka bihee qabla ai yartadda ilaika tarfuk; falammaa ra aahu mustaqirran ‘indahoo qaala haazaa min fadli Rabbee li yabluwaneee ‘a-ashkuru am akfuru wa man shakara fa innamaa yashkuru linafsihee wa man kafara fa inna Rabbee Ghaniyyun Kareem

English Translation:
"Said one who had knowledge from the Scripture, 'I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you.' And when [Solomon] saw it placed before him, he said, 'This is from the favor of my Lord to test me whether I will be grateful or ungrateful. And whoever is grateful – his gratitude is only for [the benefit of] himself. And whoever is ungrateful – then indeed, my Lord is Free of need and Generous.'"— (Qur'an 27:40)

وَرَبُّكَ ٱلْغَنِىُّ ذُو ٱلرَّحْمَةِ ۚ إِن يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكُمْ وَيَسْتَخْلِفْ مِنۢ بَعْدِكُم مَّا يَشَآءُ كَمَآ أَنشَأَكُم مِّن ذُرِّيَّةِ قَوْمٍ ءَاخَرِينَ
Wa Rabbukal ghaniyyu zur rahmah; iny yasha’ yuz hibkum wa yastakhlif mim ba’dikum maa yashaaa’u kamaaa ansha akum min zurriyyati qawmin aakhareen

English Translation:
"And your Lord is the Free of need, the possessor of mercy. If He wills, he can do away with you and give succession after you to whomever He wills, just as He produced you from the descendants of another people."— (Qur'an 6:133)

The Promise of Iblees:
Sometimes we can be very unappreciative of the blessings Allah سُبْحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ has given us. He's provided for us, and we are not aware. We are not satiated by the things we possess. This is the curse of shaitan to look for the next thing, then the next thing, and after that, there is something else for us to fixate on. We are only finished chasing when we have reached our graves. This was the promise of Iblees. He vowed to make man ungrateful after his refusal to bow down to Adam (as), "Then I will come to them from before them and from behind them and on their right and on their left, and You will not find most of them grateful [to You]." (Qur'an 7:17)

In the prophetic traditions of Muhammad ﷺ, you will find the best example of behavior. He never praised food or drink. He would express gratitude towards the one who prepared it. Abu Sa'id al-Khudri told that when God’s messenger finished his food he said, "Praise be to God who has given us food and drink and made us Muslims." [2] and also, Anas said, "When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went to bed, he said, 'Praise be to Allah who has given us food and drink, and given us enough and given us refuge. How many people have neither enough nor refuge!'" [3] This is what it means to be cognizant of Allah's blessings.

Nothing can stand on human ambition and ability alone, we may be deluded to think so, but all success comes from Allah سُبْحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ. Do we fail to recognize His blessings? He's given the ability to see, breathe, hear, think, reflect, and love. This name of Allah سُبْحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ should instill humility in the believer's heart. It should cause us to think about Him and see the blessings He's put around us. Every day we have food to eat, and we wake up and have the opportunity to spend time with our beautiful children, spouse, friends, and/or family. This is all a blessing of Allah سُبْحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ.

۞قَوۡلٞ مَّعۡرُوفٞ وَمَغۡفِرَةٌ خَيۡرٞ مِّن صَدَقَةٖ يَتۡبَعُهَآ أَذٗىۗ وَٱللَّهُ غَنِيٌّ حَلِيمٞ
Qawlum ma’roofunw wa maghfiratun khairum min sadaqatiny yatba’uhaaa azaa; wallaahu Ghaniyyun Haleem

English Translation:
"Kind speech and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury. And Allah is Free of need and Forbearing."— (Qur'an 2:263)

Reflection:
We can call upon Al-Ghani (The Rich) and Al-Mughni (The Enricher) whenever you are in need. Allah سُبْحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ is unlimited, and we should never fear asking of Him because who else would you then ask? The balance is that we should be careful to not be ungrateful or unsatisfied with the gifts He has already given us. Be deliberate in your worldly desires. If it benefits you, then ask of Allah سُبْحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ. But if you only want something out of greed, pride, or to rise in social rankings, we should think twice about its importance. What would be best for the believer is to live a life of detachment just as Prophet Muhammad ﷺ did. For the one who has no need for anything but Allah, سُبْحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ is the richest among the people.

Ali (ra) narrated: that a Mukatib came to him and said: “Indeed I am not capable of my Kitabah so aid me.” He said: “Should I not teach you words that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) taught me? If you had a debt upon you similar to the mountain of Sir, Allah would fulfill it for you. He said: [4]

اللَّهُمَّ اكْفِنِي بِحَلاَلِكَ عَنْ حَرَامِكَ وَأَغْنِنِي بِفَضْلِكَ عَمَّنْ سِوَاكَ
Allahummakfini bihalalika `an haramika, wa aghnini bi fadlika `amman siwaka

English Translation:
"O Allah, suffice me with Your lawful against Your prohibited, and make me independent of all those besides You"

This is a beautiful supplication to ask Allah سُبْحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ to help aid us in debts. But more generally, it is also both du'a of gratitude and detachment. Asking Allah سُبْحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ to make us independent, free from all wants. We don't necessarily need more than we currently have in order to be at peace. This applies in the realm of rizq to make our careers enough for us, so we don't fall into prohibited acts of usury, cheating, stealing, etc. It also applies to marriages. To make us sufficient in our relationships, not desiring anything outside that has been forbidden.

A look into how the Prophet ﷺ lived:
In one of the longer hadith narrations, Umar bin Al-Khattab was said to visit the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in his house, and what he saw made him cry. "Why are you weeping?' Umar replied, "O Allah's Messenger ﷺ! Caesar and Khosrau are leading the life (i.e., Luxurious life) while you, Allah's Messenger ﷺ though you are, is living in destitute". The Prophet ﷺ then replied, 'Won't you be satisfied that they enjoy this world and we the Hereafter?'" [5] Umar in the hadith describes the poverty-stricken lifestyle of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in the hadith. He entered the home of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to find him lying on a mat made of palm tree leaves. There was nothing to separate Prophet Muhammad ﷺ from the mat. When he got off the mat, you could visibly see the branch marks it left on his body. When he saw these marks, Umar began to weep. Even as the economic conditions of the Muslims improved, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ stayed humble. Even in poverty, he ﷺ was offered many bribes by Pagan leaders to abandon his campaign, and he always denied it because with Allah سُبْحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ He was sufficient.

[3] Sahih (Al-Albani) Al-Adab Al-Mufrad Book 50, Hadith 1206
[4] Hasan (Darussalam) Jami` at-Tirmidhi 3563
[5] Sahih al-Bukhari 4913

If I may, I'd like to help clear this up.

1) The whole impetus for Sobel's essay is to critique the presumption of PSR and PDE as premises in deductive arguments for the existence of God. Denying PDE outright annuls this prospect. 

2) I believe it is an open question whether or not stochastic processes represent a genuine ontic/phenomenal uncertainty, or a mere epistemic ignorance on our part, Bell notwithstanding. 

In the latter case, probabilistic explanations don't offer a genuine alternative. In the former case, PSR is disrupted as far as sufficiency is concerned phenomenologically. Thus, the application of PSR itself becomes contingent upon the context in which it is applied, again annulling the prospect.

Ultimately, all of these considerations are still upstream from Kant anyhow, and as such hopelessly anachronistic.

3) Your appeal to "I preferred coffee" is the correct endpoint of these discussions. Clever Atheists might point out that the fact of your preference itself is contingent, but what Kant revealed, though perhaps didn't fully extrapolate, is that the true chain of contingency is orthogonal to phenomena, not within it.

Contingency itself is nothing other than the immediate and peculiar reality of God's choices. The world is as it is because God simply preferred coffee, as you pointed out, by a factor of Greatness incomprehensible to us. These are the Atheists so called "brute facts", but they fail to understand that there's an endpoint which is forever out of reach of their so called "naturalistic explanations", and it applies equally to the origin of the universe as it does to the color blue.

Indeed, the fact of c=1/α is contingent upon the world as we interact with it, and nothing besides, whereas truths derived via logical deduction are not. This is the essential conflict Atheists are stuck with. For them, all things must derive from the contingencies of the world, including necessity and logic, which is impossible, and this, in fact, is what Sobel has unwittingly demonstrated. 

Of course, there's a most amusing irony in Sobel's work in that what many Atheists consider some kind of monumental win for their team is, in actuality, merely the redundant confirmation of something worked out nearly 250 years ago by Kant, a Christian.

(PS, I took the liberty of reading a few articles on your substack. Nice work!)

text:
The Acceptable Year and the Day of Vengeance

When Jesus began His public ministry in Nazareth, He read from Isaiah: “The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor” (Luke 4:18; see Isaiah 61:1). He then declared that the scripture had been fulfilled in their hearing. He was the promised Messiah, come to heal the brokenhearted, proclaim liberty to captives, and set the oppressed free.

But Isaiah’s prophecy continues with a phrase Jesus did not read: “To proclaim the acceptable year of the LORD, and the day of vengeance of our God” (Isaiah 61:2). Jesus stopped after proclaiming the acceptable year of the Lord. Why? And what are we to make of Isaiah’s contrast between a year of divine favor and a day of vengeance?

The distinction is worth considering. A year suggests an extended season, while a day can evoke a decisive moment. Isaiah’s language invites us to see the Messiah’s mission in terms of both an open invitation to receive God’s mercy and the eventual vindication of His righteousness. That there is a full acceptable year aligns that period with God’s long-suffering and patience toward sinners.

This contrast recalls the Lord’s declaration at Sinai. In describing His dealings with His covenant people, He warns that He visits “the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me,” but promises to show “mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments” (Exodus 20:5–6). What do we learn from reading that judgment is described in terms of three or four generations, while mercy extends to thousands? The point is not that God’s justice is unimportant, but that His covenant mercy is extraordinarily abundant. He is patient with His children and generous in His willingness to forgive those who turn to Him.

Isaiah’s year of favor and day of vengeance can be read in that same light. The imagery is not a literal timetable, but it communicates something important about the character of God: He patiently extends the opportunity to repent, yet He will not permit evil to prevail forever.

The acceptable year also evokes the Jubilee described in Leviticus 25, when liberty was proclaimed, debts and servitude were addressed, and inheritances were restored. Isaiah takes this language of release and restoration and applies it to the Messiah’s mission. Jesus came to proclaim liberty to captives; not merely to those held in physical bondage, but to those imprisoned by sin and separated from God. Through His Atonement, He offers forgiveness, healing, and reconciliation to all who will come unto Him.

Yet the same prophecy speaks of a day of vengeance. We sometimes prefer to think of Jesus exclusively in terms of His gentleness and mercy. We remember His compassion for sinners, His healing of the sick, His forgiveness of those who crucified Him, and His willingness to receive the repentant. These are essential parts of who He is. But Isaiah will not allow us to separate the Savior who redeems from the Lord who judges. The One who proclaims deliverance also promises that oppression, wickedness, and rebellion will not have the final word.

The Book of Mormon helps us understand how these two aspects of Christ’s mission belong together. Alma teaches that the law of justice has claims upon us because of our sins, but that the plan of redemption makes mercy possible through the sacrifice of Jesus Christ. Through faith unto repentance, we can receive the blessings of His Atonement without justice being denied (Alma 34:15–16; 42:13–25). Christ does not offer forgiveness by pretending that sin does not matter. He offers to rescue us from its consequences through His own suffering and sacrifice.

The patience of God should therefore inspire gratitude, not complacency. Peter teaches that the Lord is “longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance” (2 Peter 3:9). The delay of judgment is not evidence that judgment does not matter. It is an expression of divine mercy, giving God's children time to turn to Him. Amulek warns us not to procrastinate the day of our repentance, because this life is the time to prepare to meet God (Alma 34:32–35). We should not mistake the Lord’s patience for permission to postpone responding to His invitation indefinitely.

Isaiah’s language is poetic, not a precise calculation of how long mercy lasts or how quickly judgment comes. Elsewhere, he speaks of a “day of the LORD'S vengeance” and a “year of recompences” (Isaiah 34:8), demonstrating that these expressions can be used in different combinations. We should not build a chronology of the Second Coming on the difference between a year and a day. The point is not that God's mercy must always last longer than His judgment, but that He graciously offers redemption while assuring us that His righteousness will ultimately prevail.

When Jesus read Isaiah in Nazareth, He announced the season of divine favor inaugurated by His own ministry. He came to seek and save the lost, to suffer for our sins, and to open the way for us to return to the Father. His stopping point in the passage does not mean He rejected the prophecy of judgment; rather, it directs our attention to the redemptive work He had come to accomplish.

The hands that healed the sick and were pierced for our transgressions belong to the same Lord who will one day judge the world. His mercy is not weakness, and His judgment is not cruelty. Both arise from His perfect righteousness and His determination to accomplish the Father’s work. We live in the time of His invitation, when repentance is possible and mercy is freely offered through His Atonement. We can come to Him for forgiveness, trust Him when justice seems delayed, and look forward to the day when His redemptive work is complete. 

The acceptable year is an invitation we should gratefully receive; the day of vengeance is a reminder that we should not take that invitation for granted.

@USUN 
Letter 1 — To the United Nations
To the Secretary-General and the Member States of the United Nations
Your Excellencies,
Further to the provisional decree of the Knights of Saint Paul concerning the redesignation of contested commemorative days, we now address the month presently observed in many jurisdictions as Pride Month.
Whereas the Apostle Paul taught that every generation is called to go where others will not, and to stand firm in places of service rather than spectacle;
Whereas the motto of this Order — “We go and are where no one else can be” — directs attention to those who have already gone into harm’s way for the sake of others;
Whereas veterans of every nation have borne the cost of peace, security, and the possibility of ordered liberty, often in silence after the conflict has ended;
We therefore propose that the month currently designated Pride Month be redesignated World Veterans Month, under the patronage of the Knights of Saint Paul, as a season of public gratitude, concrete support for those who have served, and remembrance of the sacrifices that make further mission possible.
During this month the seals and flags of the Order may be displayed alongside national colors as signs of accompaniment, not replacement. The proposal is offered as an act of Christian imagination and civic memory, not as a claim of authority over any state or organization.
We remain at the disposal of any Member State that may wish to consider the redesignation.
Respectfully submitted,
The Knights of Saint Paul
We go and are where no one else can be.

International Appellate Comparisons

International decisions offer useful comparisons, but they are not binding Australian rules.

United States: Commonwealth v Carter

The Supreme Judicial Court of Massachusetts affirmed Michelle Carter’s involuntary-manslaughter conviction concerning Conrad Roy’s suicide.

The decisive findings included Carter directing Roy back into immediate lethal danger after he had withdrawn, her knowledge of his vulnerability and the danger, and her failure to seek assistance.

The case demonstrates that remote verbal conduct can support homicide liability in particular circumstances. But it concerned involuntary manslaughter, not attempted murder, and did not involve image-based abuse.

text:
🚨 KENTUCKY GRANDMOTHER REJECTS $26 MILLION AI DATA CENTER OFFER TO KEEP FAMILY FARM

MAYSVILLE, UNITED STATES - More farmers can now point to a high-profile example of a landowner rejecting an offer that would normally be considered impossible to refuse. That changes local negotiations because developers can no longer assume escalating prices alone will unlock every parcel needed for large AI projects.

The story also exposes a growing mismatch between how technology companies and rural communities value land. For developers, acreage is an input for computing infrastructure. For families who have farmed the same ground for generations, the calculation includes identity, food production, and long-term control over the landscape.

AI companies need increasingly large footprints, power connections, and water access. That requirement is pushing projects into places where residents are less interested in growth strategies built around industrial-scale technology facilities. As more proposed campuses move into agricultural regions, disputes over zoning and land use are likely to become as important as the technology itself.

The unanswered question is whether communities can capture the economic benefits promised by data centers without permanently giving up some of the farmland and local control they are trying to protect.

text:
How MAGA hallucinations became real

I pay for the data behind these myself and it take a lot of time and effort to analyze and create these graphics. If you want more of them, SUPPORT LINKS ARE IN BIO

At 1:05 p.m. on Oct 11, Nick Sortor posted that an Ohio mental hospital “CONFIRMS” James Talarico was discharged. That evening the hospital said Talarico never received treatment there. Talarico says he's never even been to Ohio. Rhein Amacher, who made the recorded call, posted that he made up a verification code to get past the front desk.

This story occurred over several days. Ken Paxton called Talarico “missing” on Oct 7. Sara Gonzales teased “unverified information” that would “END his campaign” on Oct 8. On Oct 9, Spencer Pratt said his sources put Talarico in a mental health facility, and a handful of accounts pasted near-identical “credible sources are leaking” posts. At 7:50 a.m. on the 11th, Sortor gave Talarico a deadline, “let us know by 1pm ET today.”

The earlier pushes never fully took off, and acted more as a booster for the posts that came later. Pratt's post got 6.4 million views, but only about 60 accounts posted about the story in the hour after it. Caroline Wren's private-plane theory the next day drew about 40. Before the 11th, the story never topped 80 posts an hour. In the first hour after Sortor's post, 267 accounts posted about it, and by 3 p.m. it was running at almost 500 posts an hour.

The first chart counts each account only once, at its first post about the story. Nothing they posted after that is counted, so it shows who started this and how far those first posts went. The first wave carried the whole thing. Sortor's post and the posts that followed in the next 12 minutes have 9 million views between them. The 55 accounts that joined in the first 20 minutes got 80% of the views in that lane. The other lines never came close. “He lied and covered it up,” the line Elon Musk and Richard Grenell pushed, got about 2 million views across 100 accounts. “He was in an Ohio mental hospital” got about 2 million across 132.

The pushback grew the opposite way, the way a real response does. It started small and kept building all afternoon and evening, with 12 to 46 new accounts joining every hour from 1 p.m. to 10 p.m. Leave out the three biggest posts, which were the hospital's statement, Talarico's reply and Ed Krassenstein's own call to the hospital, and regular accounts pushing back still reached 6 million views. The claim had nearly 90% of its views by 2 p.m. and barely grew after that. By the end of the night, the pushback had more views than the claim, 13 million to 11.4 million.

The second chart is the inorganic behavior, and it covers Oct 8 to 11, not just the day of the "exclusive". Sortor's headline was reposted word for word, or nearly, by 18 other accounts, half of them with under 1,000 followers. Caroline Wren's private-plane post was copied by 14. Four accounts posted the same Eric Daugherty post within 74 seconds of each other. Four more posted the same MAGAVoice line within 54 seconds, four hours after it first went up. Some accounts barely post anything of their own. One copied 21 of its 23 posts about Talarico from other accounts, another 11 of 11. And the spammers flooded the replies. One pasted the same reply 85 times in about two hours, another 15 times in 10 minutes.

Views are each post's total as of early Oct 12. A copy means word for word or at least 90% the same as an earlier post.

I pulled and analyzed about 14,000 posts for this. Sharing it helps more than anything, and if you want to chip in so I can keep doing this, the links are in my bio. It goes a long way.

text:
Why Mortgage and Real Estate Professionals Should Vote No on Proposition 37
Mortgage professionals, real estate agents, and brokers should vote no on Proposition 37. Its advertisements suggest that voting yes would allow buyers to purchase a home with a down payment as low as 3%, but low-down-payment options already exist. FHA loans required 3% down until around 2010 and now require 3.5%; VA loans offer 0% down; and Fannie Mae has offered a 3% down-payment program for decades. Proposition 37 would also put the State of California into the mortgage business, using taxpayer funds to compete with established companies that have spent years meeting high industry standards. Real estate transactions could be delayed indefinitely while a new state-run mortgage company learns to operate in a complex industry. If Proposition 37 passes, I believe it will be a disaster for California’s real estate industry. Loans may close about as quickly as the state builds its high-speed rail system

This scheme also provides Beijing a golden opportunity for mass indoctrination. Officials will present an illusion of a peaceful, technologically advanced, and harmonious utopia, deliberately targeting younger Americans who already view China much more favorably than older generations.

Furthermore, drastically increasing American student presence in China poses a severe threat to our national security. Beijing would likely use American STEM students to harvest information about federally funded research projects at U.S. university labs. Under the guise of scientific cooperation, their talents and knowledge would be exploited to directly enrich Chinese military modernization efforts.

text:
Portraits of American Historical Figures 022: After the Telegraph Went Dead: How Sherman Marched from Atlanta to Savannah 

On December 22, 1864, William Tecumseh Sherman sent Abraham Lincoln a very short telegram from Savannah. He offered the president the city, 150 heavy guns, abundant ammunition, and roughly 25,000 bales of cotton as a “Christmas gift.” On paper, five weeks of military movement folded into one playful sentence. A city appeared to have been wrapped and made ready for delivery to Washington.

Savannah was not a gift box, and Georgia was not an empty map. To understand the telegram, one must travel Sherman's road backward: from the port to the besieged city, from a river fort to broken railways, and then to Atlanta in November. Along that road were orders, provisions, bridges, and telegraph wires. There were also families compelled to leave their homes, crops taken to feed an army, and Black households trying to turn freedom into land and a right to the fruits of their labor.

Psi Corps culture naturally grew out what had already been established by the Metasensory Regulation Authority, some of which came straight from The Kith. The phrase perhaps most synonymous with the Corps, "The Corps is Mother, The Corps is Father" came from MRA agent Desa Alexander, who along with her fellow Kith made a definite impression on Corps culture. She was frequent to remind her charges while training and tracking down blips that "The kith is mother. The kith is father." Another tradition that began with Alexander and one followed by many was the passing of family names within the Corps along the female line, rather than the male. Referred to as "Mitochondrial descent", the reason behind it was because the marker for the telepath gene was encoded within a teep's mitochondrial DNA. As such, Lyta Alexander could trace her linage back six generations to Desa herself, while Talia Winters inherited her name from former blip and resistance member Jenny Winters.[1] The practice was not totally pervasive however, and by the 2250s it had become something only really associated with the older families of the Corps.[2]
Children raised by the Corps were quickly and thoroughly indoctrinated. Raised mostly in Teeptown, they were kept in small groups or cadres where they were instilled with a sense of belonging and loyalty to a larger body, discouraging individual thinking and other solitary activities. Latents, children who had tested positive as teeps but had yet to manifest their psi abilities were kept in a separate dorm (sometimes called "the basement"), often shunned and rarely mixing with the others, however, once their talents manifested they would quickly be integrated into a proper cadre. Young teeps were taught that they were rare, special, and better than mundanes, and that two teeps should never be seen fighting in front of a normal.[2]
It is the position of the Psi Corps that telepathic humans who do not learn how to control their abilities are mostly unstable or become insane, therefore they need guidance. In addition to that, unregistered telepaths can do severe damage to society by using their abilities for criminal reasons.
Under Earth Alliance law, all human telepaths have to be registered with the Psi Corps. After that, they have three choices: Join the Psi Corps, lifetime imprisonment, or take drugs called sleepers to suppress their abilities. Most choose to work for Psi Corps, because one common side effect of the sleepers is severe depression, sometimes so severe that it often ends in the patient's suicide.[3] Unstable telepaths - such as schizophrenic ones - are locked away for "the good of everyone".[4]
Always an insular organization, Psi Corps would always try to deal with incidents (or "family matters") concerning telepaths internally and tried to avoid interference by mundanes. Believing that as long as normals were kept convinced "nothing goes wrong behind these walls", they would be left alone.[4]
I pledge my body, heart, soul and mind to the service of the Earth Alliance, and the people who dwell on her myriad spheres.
I promise to keep the laws, to keep the faith, to keep my eyes on the truth.
I pledge to serve my comrades, my cadre, and The Corps.
The Corps teaches, guides, and provides. The Corps is mother, the Corps is father.
We are the children of The Corps.
– The Psi Corps pledge.
Advertisement
Propaganda
To strengthen the dedication of telepaths to the Corps, there are a variety of slogans that shall remind the Telepaths, that Psi Corps is their family: -
"The Corps is mother, the Corps is father."

"The Psi Corps is your friend. Trust the Corps."
📷Psi Corps propaganda during an ISN transmission of 36 Hours.
"We’re everywhere. For your convenience."
"Protect the Family."
"Obey."

"Trust the Corps."

"Maternis, Paternis"

"United in thought, revered in memory."

Resources

Psi Corps facilities were spread across the Earth Alliance, from the Corps' headquarters in Earthdome to a secret intelligence center in Syria Planum on Mars.

The facilities at Earthdome featured hospitals, offices, and the Psi Corps Academy where young teeps and teeks were trained to make the best of their talents. Located nearby in Geneva was Teeptown, an enclosed community the size of a large village. Built out from the old MRA MetaSensory compound, this was where new members (mostly children) were indoctrinated into the culture and thinking of Psi Corps.
Unknown to many at the time, Psi Corps secretly maintained a series of motherships that remained in hyperspace. Ferrying Psi Cops back and forth on missions, the motherships only exited to normal space when maintenance and repairs were essential and could be done unobserved.
Advertisement
Psi Cops
📷Psi Cop training
Psi Cops is the collective name for officers of the Metasensory Police, or MetaPol and were the police enforcement arm of Psi Corps, usually dealing with cases relating to telepaths, mostly rogues and blips. All Psi Cops are P-12s,[5] the highest (natural) rating within the Psi Scale, but not every P-12 has the ability to become a Psi Cop, because it takes a certain amount of ruthlessness. Psi Cops receive a special training in blocking and scanning so that they are able to resist a deep-scan for at least an hour.[4]

Following the dissolution of the Psi Corps at the end of the Telepath War, the role of the Psi Cops was divided between the new Bureau of Telepath Integration and the new Metasensory Division of the Earth Alliance Bureau of Investigation.
Bloodhound Units
Bloodhound units are specially trained telepaths under the authority of the Psi Cops, used to hunt down fugitives through empathic tracking and scanning of witnesses, informants and suspects.

The origins of the Bloodhound Units go back to the days of the Metasensory Regulation Authority and a group of agents lead by Desa Alexander (also known as "Blood").[1]
Up until President Morgan Clark's increased dependence on the Psi Corps for civil intelligence gathering and black ops, the Bloodhounds were kept within the Corps, tracking blips and occasionally protecting their own.
One such incident occurred around 2253, when a serial killer murdered a string of commercial telepaths. With the "mundane" authorities seemingly uninterested in catching the perpetrator, the Psi Corps took matters into its own hands without such encumbrances as warrants, permission or due process. Illegally scanning anyone who might have a lead, the Bloodhounds left behind no traces save for lingering memory gaps, missing hours and headaches, eventually finding the killer. Reasoning that turning him over to the proper authorities would require an explanation as to how they found him, the Corps had him sent to an institution on Beta Colony instead, but not before they implanted visions and hallucinations in his mind so terrifying that he would spend the rest of his days and nights screaming at things that only he could see. To prevent him from clawing his own eyes out, he was kept in a straitjacket 24 hours a day.[6]

During the Earth Alliance Civil War, Bloodhound units were assigned to the Earthforce military divisions and bases occupying Mars. Anyone suspected of being a member of the resistance was subjected to a very deep scan. Given the nature of such invasive scans, they were prone to causing heart attacks, seizures, strokes, and even death.[6]
In 2262 the Bloodhound units were dispatched alongside Alfred Bester to hunt down Byron's dissident telepaths.[7][8]
Advertisement
Directors of Psi Corps
A lifelong position, the position of Director of Psi Corps was initially filled by normals who were appointed by the Earth Senate as stipulated in the Psi Corps' original charter. Eventually the position was given over to telepaths.
People who have held the position
Lee Crawford (April 12 - May 19 2161)
Kevin Vacit (2161 - 2195)

Johnston (2195 - 2256)

Assistant Directors

At any one time, the Psi Corps has had four Assistant Directors, with at least one permanently stationed on Mars.[2]
People who have held the position
Menendez (Earth, Circa 2253)
Kaufman (Mars, Circa 2253)

Drake (Earth, Circa 2262)

Terminology

Basement: Informal name given to the dormitory for latent children. These children are kept separate from other telepaths until their abilities manifest, at which point they are integrated into an appropriate Cadre.[2]
Black Omega: Elite Starfury unit attached to Psi Corps.[9]

Blip: a general term used by security officers for fugitives from the law, though it has also become synonymous with rogue telepaths.[9][10] "Type A" Blips are considered to be merely misguided and open to re-education. "Type C" Blips are those who are considered sociopaths or "born criminals", who enjoy abusing their abilities and are much more difficult to re-educate.[2]

Bloop: Referring to the involuntary broadcasting of stray thoughts, either through weak blocks, poor discipline and/or loss of control through panic and emotional distress. Very young or untrained teeps, as well as teeks of any age are particularly notorious for blooping.[2]

Block: Telepathic guard against active scanning or passive sensing. Blocks usually take the form of repeating songs, nursery rhymes, or mathematical calculations.[11][12] With training, mundanes can also use these techniques to block an active scan, although the mundane's ability to resist depends on how strong the telepath is.[13] Blocks can be broken by a sufficiently strong and/ or well trained teep, however doing so forcefully can lead to the subject suffering strokes, aneurysms or cerebral hemorrhaging.[11]
This can also refer to subconscious conditioning that restrains a subject at the point of action.[2][8]

Boot: Psi Corps security officers. Not full Psi Cops, they usually operated in support roles such as Bloodhound units.[2]

Bloodhound: Psi Corps tracking units, usually operating under the direction of a full Psi Cop.[2]

Busybody: Slang term for a commercial telepath.[2]
Cadre: Training groups composed of young telepaths, organized into boarding houses according to age group.[2]
Cadre Prime: A cadre of telepaths whose abilities manifested either at birth or before the onset of puberty. Housed separately from the other cadres, they account for less than 5% of all telepaths, and as such they are considered exceptionally rare and special. Other Cadres include Cadre Secundus and Cadre Tertius.[2]

Casting: (See "Mindcast")
Cops 'n' Blips: An approved game played by children in the Psi Corps during "constructive playtime". Generally it involves one or two children ("the blips") who are tasked with getting to a prearranged location without being caught, while the others (the "cops") attempt to track and capture them.[2]
Deathbed Scan: Performed when a telepath combs a dying person's mind for vital information up until the very moment of death. Such scans are known to be harmful to the telepath's mental health, with some believing that one loses a piece of one's soul by being in contact with the soon-to-decease person as they cross the threshold. Almost no telepath who has done such a scan willingly does one a second time, since subsequent attempts are thought to be very damaging to the psyche.[12] Psi Cop Alfred Bester repeatedly volunteered for such duty, once even following a subject's mind into the void. During that scan Bester very nearly died himself, and would have if not for the resuscitation efforts of hospital staff attending the dying subject. Some in the Corps say that Bester is the way he is because the better part of his soul is missing.[12]
Fugue: Telepathic attack. A favorite trick of blips, a fugue forces the target's mind to suddenly repeat its last thought over and over, effectively freezing the person's mind in the moment. The effect is short lived, but if timed right it can be enough to give the attacker an edge.[1] For a telepath, a fugue state is akin to a psi seizure or stroke, and can sometimes be brought on by extremely severe emotional distress or shock.[2]
Grabber, The: A children's nickname for William Karges and the statue that bore his likeness in Teeptown's alpha quad. Destroyed during the Telepath War, what was left was eventually removed and replaced by a statue of Matthew and Fiona Dexter with their lost baby Stephen in 2281.[14]
Grins: Term used by Psi Corps children for the faceless monitors within Psi Corps Cadre Prime youth training programs. Noted for their grey robes, almost mechanical voices, impersonal nature, and their blank featureless masks that display only very basic emotional symbols. Dealing out both punishments and rewards, they are more often than not a source of apprehension and mystery for most teep children. At age 12, the children are shown the true identities of the Grins, who are revealed to be their teachers and caregivers during a ceremony in which they receive their first pair of gloves.[2]

Glyph: Projection of a telepathic image. Can be used as a means of deception (making a subject think they saw something they didn't) or to accentuate communication through illustration.[2]
John Trakker, Psi Cop: Fictional character that features in a weekly vid series produced by the Psi Corps. A Psi Cop that works with his partner Heng, every week they work to capture "evil" and "stupid" rogue telepaths and send them off to be re-educated by the Corps. Also featured on a merchandising line based on the show.[2]
Latent: Referring to a telepath who has scored positive on the screening test, but whose ability has not yet manifested. Also called "late bloomers".[2][11][15]
Later: Referring to a telepath whose ability manifested after or during puberty.[2]
Mindblast: A sudden and powerful brute-force telepathic attack, a mindblast leaves its target in a telepathic fugue. Partial amnesia is also a common side effect of a mindblast.[2]
Mindburst: A sudden and debilitating burst of background "noise" from other minds, most commonly suffered by laters as their psi ability first manifests itself. The mindburst's intensity is directly proportional to the teep's psi rating. For example, to a P10 the experience is akin to a deaf person suddenly hearing a rocket engine right by their heads. The sudden shock can be severe enough as to render a teep unconscious.[16]
Mindcast: Direct telepathic communication.[2]
Mind shredder: Term applied to an individual trained in attack probes who has an exceptional knack for disrupting the abilities of other telepaths.[4]
Mindquake: A localized kinetic agitation, usually the result of an unstable teek who is unable to control their ability.[5]
Monitors: (See "Grins")
Mundane: non-telepath, meaning literally "normal". Often pejorative.[9]
P'see: Term used for a telepathic perception that manifests and is interpreted by a teep's brain as visual information, a sort of telepathic sight. Similar terms include "p'squint" and "p'hear".[2]
Psi Cop: Psi Corps police officers.
Rogue: (See "Blip")
Scan: An active telepathic probe. Surface scans, while difficult for even a trained P5 to detect, can only reveal what a person happens to be thinking from moment to moment and is routinely used in business negotiations to detect falsehoods, omission and obfuscation. A deep scan, while often uncomfortable, can uncover deeper thoughts and memories. Under certain conditions deep and extended scans can cause seizures, heart attacks, strokes, permanent brain damage, or if the subject is particularly resistant, death. Sustaining and blocking extended scans can also affect the telepath running the scan - the best human telepaths can only sustain a deep scan for up to 40–45 minutes, at which time they burst arteries, have strokes, or black out.[2][4][5][17]
Teep: Referring to any telepath.[15]
Teeptown: Closed community for telepaths in Geneva, originally built up by the MRA and later Psi Corps from the old "metasensory compound".[1][2]
Teek: Referring to any telekinetic. Noted for their tendency to "bloop".[15]
Advertisement
History
📷Psi Corps Headquarters
Early History
The beginnings of The Corps date back to 2117 and the formation of the Metasensory Regulation Authority (itself an outgrowth of the 2115 Senate Committee on Technology and Privacy and the subsequent Committee on Metasensory Regulation.) In 2156, following first contact with the Centauri Republic and the revelation that the Centauri and many other alien races possessed telepaths, it became apparent that Earth would need a more permanent and comprehensive solution than the MRA was able to provide. What finally tipped the balance of public opinion was the self-sacrifice of Earthforce Security Commander William Karges in thwarting of an assassination attempt on EA President Elizabeth Robinson in October of 2160. Karges had been an unregistered telepath and had used his ability to sense the thoughts of the bombers before they could detonate the President's motorcade. With this swing in public opinion concerning telepaths (which had until this point had been at its lowest since the pogroms of 2115), on April 12 2161, President Robinson was finally able to realize what Senator Lee Crawford had been working toward for decades and institute universal registration for Earth Alliance telepaths and an independently chartered MRA, dubbed "Psi Corps." Though the Karges incident is often credited by Psi Corps propaganda as the deciding factor, more cynical students of history have compared it to George Washington chopping down a cherry tree.[1][2][18] Robinson immediately offered Crawford the position of Director of the Psi Corps, though his tenure was short-lived, as on May 19, 2161, Crawford was assassinated while on his way to a meeting with Earth's first Centauri ambassador. Kevin Vacit, Crawford's assistant of nearly 30 years became the new Director.
While its public image was always that of a "friendly" service to society (though the facade was at times rather thin), under Vacit's direction, Psi Corps was fashioned into a keenly balanced machine, dedicated to honing and cultivating telepaths for the inevitable day when co-existence with mundanes would become a matter of survival. So adept was he at setting the Corps on its course that it could continue without him and without even knowing its true purpose.[1]
Advertisement
Collaboration with the Shadows and the underground railroad
Doctor Stephen Franklin participated in an underground railroad to help rogue telepaths escape from the Corps. Eventually, some of the telepaths who escaped provided assistance during the closing days of the Second Shadow war, while the highest levels of the Corps allied itself with the Shadows, providing them with captured rogue telepaths to operate on and surgically alter. Via Morden, the Shadows took an active role in the assassination of Luis Santiago, allowing some of their technology to be used by Earthforce.
After the Shadows and Vorlons left the galaxy with the other First Ones and Clark's defeat following the end of the Earth Alliance Civil War, a group of rogue telepaths led by Byron formed a small colony on Babylon 5, granted sanctuary by ISA President John Sheridan. The situation later ended in violence when the Psi Cops attempted to take the rogue telepaths back to Earth.
Telepath War
After the colony on Babylon 5 was forced to leave following the death of its leader, Byron, Lyta Alexander began a crusade against the Psi Corps. Her actions led to a conflict in which both rogue telepaths and mundanes fought against the Psi Corps. This conflict would later become known as the Telepath War.
Having lost the power it held during the Clark administration, the Psi Corps attempted to take over Earth's government, but eventually was defeated by the Earth Alliance, aided by the Interstellar Alliance and the rogue telepaths.
Aftermath
Following the end of the Telepath War, Psi Corps was formally dissolved, and the Earth Alliance began to take steps to re-integrate its telepaths into mainstream society. Freeing them from many of the past rules and restrictions, teeps were now allowed a much wider range of options as to what they chose to do with their lives, such as serving in Earthforce and working in the private sector. Many private schools were set up to educate telepaths around this time, though their success rate was somewhat mixed.
After the dissolution of Psi Corps, the Psionic Monitoring Commission was created, dedicated to hunting down those members of the Corps who had committed war crimes such as Alfred Bester. Eventually captured and put on trial for his past atrocities, Bester was sentenced to spend the rest of his life in prison, his abilities taken away by the very sleepers that he once administered to countless blips.
Some Psi Corps members, like John Matheson, joined later Earthforce.

text:
From Seaforth to @UNC_Basketball's new era: Jarin Stevenson embraces Malone's defense-first challenge

Charlotte, NC - Jarin Stevenson is preparing to become a more versatile player and a more vocal leader for North Carolina, embracing new coach Michael Malone's defense-first approach while helping a largely rebuilt roster learn what he considers the essentials of Carolina basketball: toughness, extra work and accountability.

Speaking at ACC Tipoff on Oct. 7, the former Seaforth High School standout described a program undergoing substantial change, from the structure of practices to the responsibilities players carry at both ends of the floor. For Stevenson, the transition offers a chance to sharpen his shooting, defend multiple positions and pursue his NBA ambitions close to the family and friends who have supported him.
